summary: Heringsdorf Airport (HDF) is a regional airport located on the island of Usedom in northeastern Germany, serving the popular Baltic Sea seaside resorts known as the 'Kaiserbäder' (Imperial Spas), including Heringsdorf, Ahlbeck, and Bansin. Situated near the Polish border, the airport primarily handles seasonal charter and holiday flights, with increased traffic during the summer tourist season. It provides a convenient gateway to one of Germany's most elegant coastal destinations, famous for its historic spa architecture and long sandy beaches.
faqs:
Q: What towns does Heringsdorf Airport serve?
A: The airport primarily serves the Usedom island resort towns of Heringsdorf, Ahlbeck, and Bansin, collectively known as the Kaiserbäder (Imperial Spas), as well as the Polish side of the island.

Q: When is the airport busiest?
A: Heringsdorf Airport operates seasonally, with peak traffic during the summer months from May to September when tourist demand to the Baltic coast is highest.

Q: Are there customs facilities at Heringsdorf Airport?
A: Yes, the airport can handle international flights and has customs and border control services available, particularly for flights arriving from non-Schengen destinations.

Q: How far is the airport from the resort towns?
A: The airport is approximately 10 km from Heringsdorf and within 15 km of Ahlbeck and Bansin, with various ground transport options connecting them.
transport_tips: Rental cars are available at the airport and offer the most flexibility for exploring Usedom island and crossing into Poland. The Usedomer Bäderbahn (UBB) narrow-gauge railway has a stop nearby, providing scenic connections to all three Kaiserbäder towns and Świnoujście in Poland. Taxis and pre-booked shuttles can be arranged for direct transfers to your accommodation, especially useful during the busy summer season.
local_tip: If you have a few hours to spare, drive just minutes to the Polish border and visit Świnoujście—the twin city split between two countries—where you can see the historic Świnoujście Lighthouse, one of the tallest lighthouses on the Baltic coast, and enjoy surprisingly affordable Polish cuisine just across the border.
